# AI Speaking fixtures

## v2 candidate captures

These fixtures were captured from controlled synthetic Production probes on
2026-10-31. The success captures cover all six v2 operations in a one-question
Practice Part/Test flow; the final capture records the provider's HTTP 400
validation response for an invalid `part` value.

| File                                  | Operation                                      | HTTP |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ---: |
| `grading-v2-question-post.200.json`   | `POST /api/v2/speaking/questions/grading`      |  200 |
| `grading-v2-question-get.200.json`    | `GET /api/v2/speaking/responses/{response_id}` |  200 |
| `grading-v2-part-post.200.json`       | `POST /api/v2/speaking/parts/grading`          |  200 |
| `grading-v2-part-get.200.json`        | `GET /api/v2/speaking/parts/{part_result_id}`  |  200 |
| `grading-v2-test-post.200.json`       | `POST /api/v2/speaking/tests/grading`          |  200 |
| `grading-v2-test-get.200.json`        | `GET /api/v2/speaking/tests/{test_id}`         |  200 |
| `grading-v2-validation-post.400.json` | Invalid `part` on question grading             |  400 |

Every non-allowlisted string value, including transcripts, feedback, and
generated identifiers, was replaced with `[redacted]`; response keys, types,
and numeric values were retained. These are candidate provider captures, not
an approved v2 contract baseline. Per section 8 of the provider contract, the
AI Speaking owner, WISPACE, and AIHUB must approve them before the contract,
machine schema, or integration baseline is updated.

`grading.response.json` is a scrubbed successful grading. The failure
captures below come from #247. Each file name ends with the HTTP status the
provider returned.

| File                             | Status | Input                                                                  | What the provider returned                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `grading-no-speech.200.json`     | 200    | 5 s of 16 kHz mono WAV white noise; 3 s of silence gave the same shape | A normal success body with `scorability.is_scorable: false` and every band at 0, not an error                       |
| `grading-convert-audio.500.json` | 500    | About 9 KB of ASCII text uploaded as `answer.wav`                      | `{"detail": "Grading pipeline failed: [error_convert_audio] ..."}`                                                  |
| `grading-empty-audio.400.json`   | 400    | A 0-byte `answer.wav`                                                  | `{"detail": "Uploaded audio file is empty or corrupted ..."}`. AIHUB refuses audio under 100 bytes before dispatch. |

The provider's error bodies are FastAPI's `{"detail": string}`. They are not
the `ErrorResponse` (`{code, message}`) schema that its OpenAPI document
declares. The failure marker, such as `[error_convert_audio]`, appears only
inside `detail`.

In the 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-02 incidents, the provider logged
`[error_no_speech]` and AIHUB answered 502. That could not be reproduced on
2026-10-19: silence, white noise, and faint noise all returned the 200
non-scorable body above, so the provider now grades a recording without speech
instead of failing it.

## How the captures were made

On 2026-10-19 a short Node script ran inside the AIHUB production app
container and posted multipart requests straight to AI Speaking's
`POST /api/v1/speaking/grading`. It used the same base URL, the
`x-client-id`/`x-secret-key` credentials from the rendered runtime secret
bundle, and the same form fields as AIHUB's adapter:

- `user_id=aihub-capture-247`
- `part=1`
- `question_id=p1_hometown`
- `test_type=Practice`

All audio was generated by the script, so no candidate content was involved.
To repeat a capture, build the same request with a generated file.

Before a body is stored, replace every transcript, word, phoneme, and
Vietnamese text value with `[redacted]`, and replace session and test IDs with
a fixed placeholder. Keep the keys, types, numbers, and failure markers.
`src/downstream/speaking/speaking-provider-fixtures.spec.ts` fails if any
`grading*.json` here contains Vietnamese text or an unredacted transcript
field.
